neighbours.label: the point where a quoted statement or reported text ends or is introduced (closing quote plus newline, 'stating', 'read')
fire:
The sign at the entrance read, “No dogs allowed beyond this point.”
We turned back.

A note on the fridge said, “Back at six, dinner is in the oven.”
She smiled.

The letter ended with a line stating, “We regret to inform you.”
He sat down.

“This was the best party we have ever had, thank you!”
- “The music was great.”

Her post read: “Please share this with anyone who can help.”
It spread quickly.
The label carried a warning stating that the product is flammable.

The coach told reporters, “We will be back next season.”
The crowd cheered.
The headline read “Town Floods Again” and the article followed below.
quiet: The sign at the entrance was old and covered in moss, so we turned back.
A note on the fridge was half hidden behind a magnet, and she smiled.
The letter was written on thin blue paper, and he sat down to read.
This was the best party we have ever had, and the music was great.
Her post was shared by hundreds of people, and it spread quickly.
The label was printed in small letters on the back of the bottle.
The coach met reporters after the game, and the crowd cheered.
The newspaper covered the flood on its front page with a large photo.

notes: Card: '.”\n' x7, '.\n' x3, 'sic' x4, ' stating', ' read' (a post read), ' say'. Weak pole (max 6.8).
